name: Standing hip abduction
summary: Side leg raise for glute medius — the sideways banded kick, and the muscle that keeps the pelvis level when you walk and run.
setup: Stand facing the camera, about 2.5 m away, camera at hip height, one hand lightly on a chair or wall. Whole body in frame. To progress, loop a band around both ankles. Lift one leg straight out to the side and lower with control; do all reps on one leg, then repeat facing the camera with the other.
brief: Stand tall, one hand lightly on a chair or wall. Lift the working leg straight out to the side, then lower it with control.
why: From the front, the leg swings across the camera plane, so raise angle, pelvis tilt, trunk lean and knee bend are all read directly with nothing in the way.

guide.surface: Standing on a firm floor, barefoot or in flat shoes. A chair back, counter or wall within reach of one hand.

points.t: Stand tall on the standing leg, weight through the middle of the foot, knee straight but not locked back.
Both feet point straight ahead. As the leg lifts the working foot stays pointing forward — toes do not turn up to the ceiling. Turning the foot out switches the work to the hip flexors.
Working leg lifts straight out to the side, in line with the body, not drifting forward.
Knee straight throughout; lead with the heel.
To add load, loop a resistance band around both ankles (start yellow/light; move up a colour when 15 clean reps are easy). The band must not pull the standing leg over — if it does, go lighter.
Raise to 25–35°: about 30–40 cm off the floor for most people. Higher than this the pelvis has to tilt.
Lower under control to just above the floor, then lift again without resting the foot.
Pelvis level and facing forward. Imagine a glass of water balanced on each hip bone.
No sway or hitch: the hip of the working leg should not pop up as the leg lifts.
Torso upright and still; ribs stacked over the pelvis. Leaning the trunk away makes the leg look higher without the glute doing more.
Gently brace the abdominals as if about to be nudged.
Fingertips of one hand resting lightly on the support — for balance only, not weight. Gripping and leaning on it hides trunk lean and takes load off the glute.
Other hand on the hip (to feel the pelvis stay level) or hanging relaxed.
Eyes forward at the camera, chin level. Looking down at the leg tips the trunk.
Breathe out as the leg lifts, in as it lowers.
2 s up, brief pause, 2 s down. No swinging.

guide.stop: Pinching at the front of the hip, low-back pain, or you cannot keep balance without gripping the support.

tempo: 2 s up, brief pause, 2 s down.
progression: Band around the ankles; slower lowering.
regression: Smaller raise; fingertips on a wall.
contraindications: Pinching at the front of the hip or low-back pain.

faults.label: Leaning away to lift higher
faults.tip: Leaning the trunk away makes the leg look higher without the glute doing the work. Keep the torso upright and accept a smaller raise.

faults.label: Knee bending
faults.tip: Lead with the heel and keep the knee locked so the movement comes from the hip.

faults.label: Hip hiking
faults.cue: Hips level — lift from the hip
faults.tip: The pelvis should stay level; lifting the hip on the working side uses the back muscles instead of the glute. (The camera sees some pelvis tilt on every raise; only a tilt well beyond what the raise explains is flagged.)

faults.label: Standing knee bending
faults.cue: Stand tall on the standing leg
faults.tip: A bent standing knee lets the pelvis drop and the trunk lean. Keep it straight but not locked.

faults.label: Swinging too high
faults.tip: Above about 45° the pelvis has to tilt; keep the raise modest and slow.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Aim for the raise target without leaning; if it is not reachable, lower the target rather than cheat.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.cue: Slower — two seconds up, two down
faults.tip: Momentum does the work if the leg swings. Two seconds up, brief pause, two seconds down.
